clue.text: Get even with someone and overcome the backlog?

definitions.meaning: to draw level with a person who was ahead of you
to clear arrears of work that have piled up

explanation.surface: Someone wants revenge on a rival and also to clear their overflowing in-tray.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both drawing level with a leader and clearing accumulated arrears of work.

clue.text: A bar etc prepared for the entertainment

indicators.note: prepared means worked into a new form, so the letters of the fodder are rearranged

explanation.surface: Staff get a pub ready for an evening's show.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabaret is a show of songs and sketches put on in a nightclub or restaurant.

clue.text: Unusually blunt? True, being upset

indicators.note: unusually means arranged in an odd way, so these two words' letters are shuffled together

explanation.surface: Someone is told a blunt truth and gets upset by it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is a link word joining the anagram to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Turbulent describes a disturbed, agitated state, a fair synonym for being upset.

clue.text: Wearing socks, those darned ones included

indicators.note: included tells us the letters sit inside the run of words those darned

explanation.surface: Someone is wearing socks, including the ones they have mended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ones' is padding for the surface; the letters straddle the end of 'those' and the start of 'darned'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosed is an old word for clad in hose, that is stockings or socks.

clue.text: Chicken-feed? Rather more than that

parts.note: chicken-feed usually means a trivial sum of money; here read literally, food for livestock in general, which is rather more than a few grains for hens

explanation.definitionFit: Provender is dry food for livestock, such as hay or grain, of which chicken-feed is one kind.

clue.text: Bar corner including English kind of seat

indicators.note: including means the word for bar takes the abbreviation for English inside it

parts.note: to bar is to ban
to corner something is to bag or secure it

explanation.surface: In a corner of a pub sits an English-style seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A beanbag is a large floppy cushion filled with beads, used as a seat.

clue.text: It accompanies you after a sneeze

definitions.text: It accompanies you after a sneeze

parts.words: It accompanies you after a sneeze
parts.note: the word customarily said just before 'you' when someone sneezes

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to call divine favour on someone, as in the polite response to a sneeze.

clue.text: Large number of trunks etc in this place

definitions.text: Large number of trunks etc in this place

parts.words: Large number of trunks etc in this place
parts.note: trunks suggests luggage or swimwear, but these are tree trunks, growing together in a collection

explanation.definitionFit: An arboretum is a garden or park where many kinds of trees are grown for study and display.

clue.text: British border mark

parts.note: a rand is a strip or border, as of leather on a shoe

explanation.surface: A frontier between British territories is marked.
explanation.definitionFit: A brand is an identifying mark burned onto livestock or goods.

clue.text: Braggarts with boastful talk on studies

indicators.note: in a down clue on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: gas is empty, boastful talk
to con is to study or learn by heart, so cons are studies

explanation.surface: Braggarts bring their bluster to bear on academic studies.
explanation.definitionFit: Gascons, natives of Gascony, were proverbially boastful, so the word came to mean braggarts.

clue.text: Poet with boon (asset) set out makes irrevocable move

parts.note: Robert Burns was the Scottish national poet

indicators.note: set out means laid out afresh, so the letters of the bracketed pair are rearranged

explanation.surface: A poet, given a boon, sets out his assets and makes a bold, irrevocable move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word. The idiom recalls invaders burning their ships so retreat was impossible.
explanation.definitionFit: To destroy every means of retreat is to commit oneself beyond turning back.

clue.text: See 9
Shown by halo about the head?

definitions.text: Shown by halo about the head?

parts.words: Shown by halo about the head?
parts.note: a halo is a ring; the property it displays is its circular shape, not saintliness

explanation.definitionFit: Roundness is the quality of being circular, as a ring of light is.

clue.text: Set advertisement in capital city

indicators.note: in means the short word for advertisement is placed inside the city name

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro, the former Brazilian capital, is often shortened to Rio

explanation.surface: An advertisement is placed in a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: A radio set is a receiver, so set can stand for the device.

clue.text: Amount of heat, very large, escaping from the flask

indicators.note: escaping from means those letters leave the flask's name

parts.note: a Thermos is a vacuum flask, a trade name
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize, very large

explanation.surface: A great deal of heat escapes from a vacuum flask.
explanation.definitionFit: A therm is a unit of heat, used in the UK for billing gas supply.

clue.text: Building society, say, meet aggro if wrong

indicators.note: if wrong means the letters are put in the wrong order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A building society faces trouble if things go wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A building society is a British savings and home-loan institution, an example of a lender holding a home loan.

clue.text: Slow ball — don't panic, strike!

indicators.note: panic suggests wild disorder, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: a ball is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A bowler sends down a slow ball and tells himself to stay calm and get a wicket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' reads as a cricket or bowling term but is the industrial action.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop work as a protest is what workers do when they walk out on strike.

clue.text: Two items useful for gardener as a dividing line

parts.note: a gardener needs water for plants and a shed for tools; the phrase supplies both pieces
a gardener needs water for plants and a shed for tools; the phrase supplies both pieces

explanation.surface: A gardener lists two handy things, and they mark a boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: A watershed is the ridge dividing river basins, and figuratively a turning point.

clue.text: To get a bigger figure have more than the rest!

definitions.text: To get a bigger figure have more than the rest!

parts.words: To get a bigger figure have more than the rest!
parts.note: read as out plus number, it suggests beating a figure; really it means having greater numbers than others

explanation.definitionFit: To exceed others in quantity is to be more numerous than them.

clue.text: Is the printer pretending partly to produce clarification?

indicators.note: partly means only a portion of the run printer pretending is used

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the printer is feigning in order to explain something.
explanation.definitionFit: To interpret is to explain or make clear the meaning of something.

clue.text: A moment in the present month

definitions.meaning: in old business letters 'the 5th inst.' meant the fifth of this month

explanation.surface: Something happens in a flash during this current month.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun means a very brief time, and as a formal term means of the current month.

clue.text: Car's time in the wide open space

definitions.note: the definition is car, with 's standing for is

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation for time goes inside the word for open land

parts.note: a moor is a wide stretch of open, uncultivated upland

explanation.surface: A car spends its time out on the open moorland.
explanation.definitionFit: Motor is an informal British word for a car.

clue.text: It helps the motorist in many ways

definitions.text: It helps the motorist in many ways

parts.words: It helps the motorist in many ways
parts.note: it sounds like general praise, but the item literally shows many ways, that is roads

explanation.definitionFit: A road map shows the routes a driver can take.

clue.text: Nag's left for transport, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: for transport means the letters are carried into a new arrangement

parts.note: the word Nag's spelt with its s gives four letters

explanation.surface: A horse is left behind as transport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang is informal, nonstandard vocabulary, a particular style of talking.

clue.text: The chambers one artist filled with books

indicators.note: filled with means the pair of pieces takes the abbreviation for books inside

parts.note: A is the indefinite article, meaning one
RA, Royal Academician, is the usual abbreviation for an artist
NT, New Testament, is a collection of books

explanation.surface: An artist's rooms are filled with books.
explanation.definitionFit: Antra is the plural of antrum, an anatomical cavity or chamber, especially in bone.

clue.text: Half the hecklers and copper meet attorney (a big fish)

indicators.note: half means only the first five of the ten letters of the word for hecklers are kept

parts.note: barrackers are hecklers, those who jeer at a speaker
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
DA is the US abbreviation for district attorney

explanation.surface: Some hecklers and a police officer meet a lawyer, who is a big shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' and 'meet' are link words. 'Copper' suggests a policeman but is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: The barracuda is a large, predatory tropical sea fish.

clue.text: Lip-applied to this section?

parts.note: lip suggests cheek, but in an orchestra the lips are pressed to mouthpieces in this group of instruments

explanation.definitionFit: The brass section is played by buzzing the lips into a mouthpiece, a technique called embouchure.

clue.text: A warning sound in the Territorial Army

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit within the words Territorial Army

explanation.surface: A warning is sounded among the volunteer soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army was Britain's volunteer reserve force. 'the' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarm is a signal such as a bell or siren that warns of danger.

clue.text: Famous people put their hands to it

definitions.text: Famous people put their hands to it

parts.words: Famous people put their hands to it
parts.note: put their hands to suggests taking up a task; here celebrities write their signatures in a fan's book

explanation.definitionFit: A book kept for collecting signatures of famous people.

clue.text: See 25
People who make fun of difficult problems

definitions.meaning: those who tease or mock others playfully
puzzles or brain-twisters that are hard to solve

explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers both those who mock playfully and tricky puzzles, as in brain-twisters.

clue.text: I'm back acquiring runs in the outfield, being a hooker

indicators.note: in means the reversed word plus the abbreviation sits inside the fielding position

parts.note: deep is the area of the field far from the batsman, the outfield

indicators.note: back means the word I'm, without its apostrophe, is read backwards

parts.note: I'm gives the letters I and M
acquiring means the reversed piece takes on the runs abbreviation after it

explanation.surface: A cricketer returns to field in the deep after scoring runs, posing as a hooker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is a link word. 'Hooker' suggests a rugby forward or a batsman's hook shot but means a prostitute.
explanation.definitionFit: Demirep is an old word for a woman of doubtful reputation, a courtesan or prostitute.
